questions.q: What is the real test for whether something should be modeled as a Configuration Item?
options: Whether it cost the company money
Whether its state, configuration, and relationships need to be tracked for delivering and managing services
Whether it has a serial number
Whether it appears on an Incident form
questions.explain: A CI is defined by whether tracking its state and relationships matters for managing services — not by cost, a serial number, or any single form.

questions.q: Which of these is NOT a Configuration Item?
options: A physical application server
A specific installation of an application
An Incident record describing an outage
A network switch
questions.explain: An Incident is a work record on the task table — it represents something being done, not something that exists. It references a CI; it is not one.

questions.q: How does an Incident record actually relate to a Configuration Item?
options: The Incident becomes a CI once it's resolved
There is no real connection between work records and CIs
An Incident's `cmdb_ci` field is a reference field pointing at the specific CI affected
A CI is deleted automatically when its related Incident is closed
questions.explain: The `cmdb_ci` field on a work record is a reference field — it points at a CI record; the two stay separate records with separate lifecycles.

questions.q: What happens to a CI when the Incident that referenced it is closed?
options: The CI is archived along with the Incident
The CI keeps existing independently — closing the Incident doesn't affect the CI record
The CI's `cmdb_ci` field is cleared
The CI is automatically marked as a work record
questions.explain: A CI represents something that exists independent of any work happening to it. Its lifecycle is separate from any Incident, Change, or Problem that references it.

questions.q: Which earlier lesson in this path first introduced Configuration Item as an ITIL practice, rather than as a ServiceNow table?
options: Platform Fundamentals Lesson 12, The Task Table Hierarchy
ITIL 4 Foundations Lesson 23, Service Configuration Management Practice
Platform Fundamentals Lesson 11, Base Tables & Table Extension
This is the first time the concept has appeared anywhere in this path
questions.explain: ITIL 4 Foundations Lesson 23 introduced the practice conceptually; Platform Fundamentals Lesson 11 later named the actual `cmdb_ci` table behind it.
